transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess it’s not anything too dramatic, but I’ve noticed I’m having trouble keeping up when people are talking to me. Like at the museum, someone will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, trying to listen, but then I realize I missed a chunk in the middle and I have to ask them to repeat it. It’s a little embarrassing, honestly.
When this happens, does it feel like you heard the sounds but couldn’t make out the words?

Not exactly like I couldn’t make out the words, no. It’s more like… someone at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’m looking at them and trying to follow, but then I realize I missed the middle part somehow. So I end up asking them to run it by me again. It’s not all the time, but enough that I noticed it, if that makes sense.
Does this kind of missing the middle happen when you’re reading, too?

Yeah, I think it can, a little. Like if I’m reading a gallery packet or some notes, I’ll start off fine, and then after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going over the words but my mind’s kind of drifted. Then I have to go back and read the same part again. It’s not like I can’t read it, I just… lose the thread sometimes, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

I don’t think so, not a lot. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around anxious for no reason. At least, I haven’t really noticed that being a big part of it. Does that answer what you mean?
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yes, I think so… though I probably would’ve called it just being a bit dreamy back then. In grade school, my report cards sometimes said things like “daydreams” or “needs reminders to finish work.” And my mother used to sit beside me while I did homework, just to keep me on track, before I was twelve. It wasn’t like I was trying to be difficult, I don’t think… I just needed nudging. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Not really, no… I mean, I still enjoy the usual things when I get to them. Maybe I have quieter days, but I wouldn’t say things have stopped being enjoyable. I don’t think that’s been a big problem for me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often forget everyday things, like appointments, errands, or where you put items?

Yes… I suppose I do, more than I’d like to admit. It’s usually not big things, but I’ll put something down “somewhere safe,” like a camera battery, a name tag, or an envelope with sign-up sheets, and then I spend half the morning retracing my steps trying to find it. It’s embarrassing, really. I try to be organized, but those little things do get away from me. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do these attention problems also cause difficulties in more than one part of your life, such as both at work and at home?

Yes… I think it does, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I’m not working now, but with the museum group, some of the planning bits have sort of… quietly been shifted away from me, I think because I wasn’t keeping on top of them as well as I should.

And at home it shows up too, in small ways. I’ve also stopped feeling as confident leading the art walks as I used to, which bothers me. I’m still managing, mostly, but yes… it’s not just in one place. Is that a fair way to put it?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task all the way through, especially if it isn’t very interesting to you?

Yes… I think that happens. Not always, but enough that I notice it.

Like, I can sit down with a gallery packet or some notes and I start off perfectly fine, thinking I’ll just get through it. Then after a few minutes I realize my eyes are still going over the page, but my mind has gone somewhere else entirely. So I have to go back and read the same bit again.

It’s a little frustrating, but I do usually get there eventually. Does that count as trouble staying focused?
Do you often put off tasks because they require a lot of sustained mental effort?

Yes… I do, though I don’t like to think of it as avoiding exactly. It’s more that if I know I need to sit down and read through a long exhibit description, or plan out what I’m going to say for a talk, I suddenly notice all sorts of little chores around the house that “need” doing first.

I’ll tell myself I’m just clearing the decks, but really, sitting with all that reading can feel like pulling teeth. I do get to it eventually, usually, but I can put it off longer than I should. Does that sound like what you mean?
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details, even when you know the material?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who makes a lot of careless mistakes, at least not that people are pointing out to me.

I might miss a detail here or there, but… I suppose everyone does that sometimes. If you mean things like knowing the material but still overlooking something obvious, I can’t say I’ve noticed that as a big pattern. Is that alright to say?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping your materials in order?

I don’t know that I’d say that’s a big problem for me. I mean, I’m not perfectly organized or anything, but I haven’t really noticed it causing much trouble.

My papers or things at home might get a bit scattered now and then, but… I usually know roughly where things are, or I can sort them out if I need to. So I’m not sure I’d count that one, unless you mean something more specific?
Do people often tell you that you seem not to listen when they’re speaking to you directly, even when there isn’t an obvious distraction?

Yes, that does happen sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m ignoring people, because I’m really not trying to.

At the museum, someone might be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking at them, nodding along, and then suddenly I realize I’ve missed the middle part of what they said. Then I have to ask them to run it by me again. It’s a bit embarrassing, honestly. Does that count?
Have these attention problems caused significant problems in your daily functioning?

I guess… yes, a bit. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still manage day to day. But with the museum group, I’ve noticed they’ve sort of quietly moved some of the planning pieces away from me.

No one’s been unkind about it, but I can tell. And I’ve stopped feeling as confident leading the art walks the way I used to. I hate saying that, because I liked being someone they could count on, but… yes, I suppose it has affected things some.
Do you often start tasks but have trouble finishing them, even when you understand what needs to be done?

Yes… I think that happens, though I try not to let it. If someone in the volunteer group gives me a few things to take care of, I’ll usually get the first part done — like printing the maps — but then I might forget to call the museum desk, or I’ll leave the folders sort of half-ready until someone reminds me.

It’s not that I don’t understand what needs doing. I do. I just… don’t always carry it all the way through unless there’s a nudge. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions and finishing tasks, even when you understand what needs to be done?

Yes, I suppose so… not every time, but often enough that I notice it.

Like with the volunteer group, if someone gives me a few things to handle, I’ll usually start off fine. I might print the maps, for example, and feel like I’m on top of it. But then I’ll forget to call the museum desk, or I’ll leave the folders only half put together until someone gives me a reminder.

I do understand what they’re asking me to do. It’s more that I don’t always follow it all the way through on my own. I’m not sure if that’s exactly what you mean, but that’s the sort of thing that happens.
Do these kinds of attention lapses happen often—on most days?

Most days… yes, I think so. Not all day long or anything, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it does come up pretty regularly.

With the volunteer group especially, if I’m given a few things to handle, I’ll do the first part — like getting the maps printed — and then somehow the next piece slips, like calling the museum desk or finishing the folders. Usually it gets caught when someone reminds me. So… yes, I’d say often enough to be most days in some form.
